ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.claim: Night prayer is the remedy for the anxiety in the address and brings blessings that renew energy and strengthen faith and resolve.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.anchor: this prayer rejuvenates his energy and strengthens his faith and resolve

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r3.claim: The Qur’an should be recited in a slow, measured manner during the prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r3.anchor: it should be read in slow measured tones

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r4.claim: The Prophet recited melodiously, paused at verses, sometimes repeated them emotionally, sought refuge at warnings, thanked God at mercy, and prostrated when prompted; reflective recitation follows Qur’anic guidance, unlike reward-only recitation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r4.anchor: with a melodious and tuneful voice

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r1.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r1.claim: ʿAli says Quran recitation should be clear, not scattered or shaken like poetry; readers should pause at its wonders, move hearts, and avoid aiming only to finish a sura.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r1.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سئل عن قول الله { ورتل القرآن ترتيلا } قال بينه تبيينا

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r2.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r2.claim: A parallel al-Kafi version says to pour the Quran into hard hearts, avoid shaking it like poetry or scattering it like sand, and not make the sura's end the only goal.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r2.anchor: عن الصادق عن علي عليه السلام ولفظ بينه تبيينا ولا تهذه هذ الشعر

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r3.speaker: رسول الله
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r3.claim: The Prophet says the best recitation is that which makes a listener see that the reader fears God.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r3.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أي الناس أحسن قراءة قال الذي إذا سمعته يقرأ

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r4.claim: Al-Sadiq says not to read hastily; when a verse mentions Paradise or Hell, pause to ask for Paradise or seek God's protection from Hell.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي حمزة قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام إن القرآن لا يقرأ هذرمة ولكن يرتل ترتيلا

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r5.speaker: أبو بصير
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r5.claim: Abu Basir explains tartil as taking one's time and improving the voice.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r5.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال هو أن تتمكث فيه وتحسن به صوتك

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r6.speaker: أم سلمة
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r6.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet divided his recitation verse by verse.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r6.anchor: عن ام سلمة أنها قالت " كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقطع قراءته آية آية

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r7.speaker: أنس
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r7.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet lengthened his voice in recitation.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال " كان صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يمد صوته مدا

TABATABAI:73:1-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r8.speaker: رسول الله
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r8.claim: Asked how revelation came, the Prophet describes a bell-like sound that is hardest on him, then fades after he has understood it, or an angel appearing as a man; ʿAisha reports bodily effects during revelation.
TABATABAI:73:1-19/r8.anchor: سأل الحارث بن هشام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال يا رسول الله كيف يأتيك الوحي

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r6.claim: Tartīl means arranging something well and clearly, without flaw, and fully delivering what is due; distinct, well-ordered teeth and measured, composed speech illustrate the term.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r6.anchor: “Tertîl” bir şeyi güzel tensik ve tertib ile kusursuz olarak açık açık hakkını îfâ ederek tebyin eylemektir

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r7.claim: Quranic tartīl gives every letter, pronunciation, arrangement, and meaning its full due; the emphatic verbal noun tartīlan demands the finest degree of recitation.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r7.anchor: Kur’ân’ın tertîli de böyle her harfinin, edâsının, nazmının, mânasının hakkını doyura doyura vererek okunmasıdır

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r8.claim: A beautiful text loses its beauty when badly recited, and readers who cannot recite well can ruin good words.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r8.anchor: Bir söz haddizâtında ne kadar güzel olursa olsun gereği gibi güzel okunmayınca güzelliği kalmaz

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r9.claim: Tartīl is not arbitrary singing that stretches and bends sounds like a string instrument; it requires tajwīd guided by meaning, eloquence, and spiritual fit.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r9.anchor: sade ses güzelliğiyle gelişigüzel eze büze tegannî etmek

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r10.claim: Tajwīd varies force and softness, length and shortening, nasalization and clear pronunciation, concealment and assimilation, connection and pause, to understand and convey the meaning.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r10.anchor: bütün maksad mânayı duymak ve mümkin olduğu kadar duyurmak olmak üzere tecvid ile okumak işidir

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r11.claim: Tajwīd is necessary, but perfecting articulation by cracking the qāf must not obscure the meaning.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r11.anchor: Tecvid de kaf çatlatmak derdiyle çatlatmaktaki mânayı gayb etmek değildir

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r1.claim: Qurʾānic recitation has three tempos: tahqīq is very slow, tedvīr moderate, and hadr fast, measured by the length of elongation.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r1.anchor: Kur’an kıraati üç mertebe üzere tasnif olunmuştur: Tahkik, tedvir, hadr.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r2.claim: The author assigns ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and Warsh from Nāfiʿ to tahqīq; Ibn ʿĀmir and Kisāʾī to tedvīr; the rest to hadr, while every mode must preserve each letter and vowel fully.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r2.anchor: Âsım, Hamza, Nâfi‘den Verş kıraatleri tahkik, İbn Âmir, Kisâî kıraatleri tedvir

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r3.claim: All recitation modes require tartīl in its essential sense; the later command to recite what is easy permits the faster tempos.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r3.anchor: asıl mânasıyla tertil hepsinde şarttır. Böyle hadr ve tedvir taksîmine cevaz veren ise gelecek olan

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r4.claim: The first purpose of rising at night is measured Qurʾānic recitation; although it also covers teaching and recitation beyond prayer, rising in this context ordinarily means prayer.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r4.anchor: burada tertîl-i Kur’an emri kıyamdan ilk maksad bu olduğunu gösterir.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r5.claim: Because little Qurʾān had yet been revealed, prolonged nightly recitation trained the Prophet for worship and application, rather than serving merely as memorization.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r5.anchor: henüz çok bir şey nâzil olmadığı cihetle her gece bu kadar uzun müddet kalkıp da Kur’an tertil etmek bunun mücerred bellemek için değil

NAHHAS:v5p55/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p55/r12.claim: The واو in أو انقص is vocalized with damma to separate adjacent sukuns, or with kasra according to the original pattern.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r12.anchor: ( أو انقص منه قليلا ) ضمت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين وإن شئت كسرت على الأصل

NAHHAS:v5p55/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r13.speaker: الأصمعي
NAHHAS:v5p55/r13.claim: Al-Asma'i compares ترتيل to well-spaced teeth, where gaps remain and the teeth do not overlap.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r13.anchor: قال الأصمعي وفي الأسنان الرتل وهو أن يكون بين الأسنان الفرج لا يركب بعضها بعضا

NAHHAS:v5p55/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p55/r14.claim: Al-Nahhas accepts the established sense: pause in recitation, separate each letter from the next, and do not rush them together.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r14.anchor: حقيقته في كلام العرب تلبث في قراءته وافصل الحرف من الحرف الذي بعده ولا تستعجل

NAHHAS:v5p55/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r15.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p55/r15.claim: Another derivation takes رتل as weakness and gentleness, so the command means to make recitation gentle and avoid rushing.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r15.anchor: وقيل هو من الرتل الذي هو الضعف واللين فالمعنى لين القراءة ولا تستعجل بالانكماش

ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r8.claim: Ratt il means to make the recitation clear; this requires fully articulating every letter rather than rushing.
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r8.anchor: بينه تبيينا، والتبيين لا يتم بأن يعجل في القرآن، إنما يتم بأن تبين جميع الحروف وتوفي حقها في الإشباع

ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r1.claim: Following Jawhari, Baydawi, Lisan al-'Arab, and Qamus, Asad defines tartil as distinct, orderly, unhurried arrangement; in recitation it is calm, measured delivery that considers the meaning.
ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r1.anchor: The term tartil primarily denotes "the putting [of something] together distinctly, in a well-arranged manner, and without any haste"

ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r2.claim: A variant of the phrase in 25:32 has a somewhat different sense, describing the manner in which the Qur'an was revealed.
ASAD-NOTES:73:1#n3/r2.anchor: A somewhat different significance attaches to a variant of this phrase in 25:32, applying to the manner in which the Qur'an was revealed.

QIRAAT-ER:73:4:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:73:4:6#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:73:4:6#1/r1.claim: The hmz reading drops hamza between vowels, changing qurʾān to qurān with phonetic smoothing but no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:73:4:6#1/r1.anchor: Hamza dropped: qurʾān → qurān; simplification of hamza between vowels — no semantic change but phonetic smoothing

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says it reached him that the Prophet generally lengthened his recitation.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#3/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ورتل القرآن ترتيلا ﴾ قال بلغنا أن عامة قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت المد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r1.claim: The conjunction and pronoun work as in the preceding construction, regardless of which of the two main parses is chosen.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r1.anchor: عطف كما سبق وكذا الكلام في الضمير ولا يختلف على القولين فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r2.claim: The Prophet is given a choice to pray half the night, less than half, or more than half.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r2.anchor: وهو تخيير صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بين أن يقوم نصف الليل أو أقل من النصف أو أكثر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r3.claim: The better measure for increase or decrease is the half that includes the portion prayed, rather than the unprayed half, though the amounts are equal.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r3.anchor: رجح الأول بأن فيه جعل معيار النقص والزيادة النصف المقارن للقيام وهو أولى من جعله للنصف العاري منه بالكلية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r4.claim: Some parse half as a substitute for the remainder of the night after the exception, with both pronouns referring to that remainder.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r4.anchor: وجعل بعضهم الإبدال من الليل الباقي بعد الثنيا والضميرين له

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that if the pronoun refers to the little, the result is an unintelligible exception of half of an unspecified little; if it refers to the night, the first exception becomes redundant.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r6.anchor: وكذا اعترض أبو حيان ذلك الإبدال بقوله أن ضمير نصفه حينئذ إما أن يعود على المبدل منه أو على المستثنى منه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r7.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r7.claim: A response says the exception remains useful because reducing one half implies reducing the other, eases the vigil, contrasts worship with free time, and clarifies after initial ambiguity.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r7.anchor: إن فيه تنبيها على تخفيف القيام وتسهيله لأم قلة أحد النصفين تلازم قلة الآخر وتنبيها على تفاوت ما شغل بالطاعة وما خلا منها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r8.speaker: السمين
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r8.claim: Al-Samīn replies that calling the exception unknown is wrong: the night and its halves are known, and an unspecified part may be excepted from a known whole.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r8.anchor: وتعقب السمين الشق الأول أيضا بأن قوله استثناء مجهول من مجهول غير صحيح لأن الليل معلوم وكذا بعضه من النضف وما دونه وما فوقه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r9.claim: Despite the objections and replies, the author relies on his earlier analysis as the sound basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r9.anchor: ومع هذا المعول عليه ما سلف وجوز أن يكون نصفه بدلا من الليل بدل بعض من كل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r10.claim: Another fronting-and-postponement parse takes half as a partitive substitute for night: the options then amount to half, a third, or a quarter of the night.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r10.anchor: والكلام على نية التقديم والتأخير والأصل قم نصف الليل إلا قليلا وضمير منه وعليه للأقل من النصف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r11.claim: On that analysis, pray less than half, decrease that amount a little, or increase it a little; examples yield one-third, one-quarter, or half.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r11.anchor: فكأنه قيل قم أقل من نصف الليل بأن تقوم ثلث الليل أو أنقص من ذلك الأقل قليلا بأن تقوم ربع الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r12.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r12.claim: Al-Kashshaf construes the choice as less than half but more than a third, with neither decrease nor increase reaching the adjacent full fraction.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r12.anchor: وفي الكشاف ما يفهم منه على ما قيل أن التخيير فيما وراء النصف أي فيما يقل عن النصف ويزيد على الثلث

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r13.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r13.claim: Al-Kashf says the increase stays below half and the decrease above a third because otherwise clear fraction names should have been used; the author considers this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r13.anchor: وإنما جعل الزيادة دون النصف والنقصان فوق الثلث لأنهما لو بلغا إلى الكسر الصحيح لكان الأشبه أن يذكر بصريح اسميهما

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r14.claim: Some take the named fractions of a third, quarter, and half as examples rather than an exhaustive set of permitted amounts.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r14.anchor: وظاهر كلام بعضهم أن ذكر الثلث والربع والنصف فيه على سبيل التمثيل لا أن الأقل والأنقص والأزيد محصورات فيما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r15.claim: A further fronting parse refers both pronouns to half, making the choice between a definite amount below half and either a decrease from or increase over half.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r15.anchor: وجوز أيضا كون الكلام على نية التقديم والتأخير كما مر آنفا لكن مع جعل الضميرين للنصف لا للأقل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r16.claim: One argument says the lesser amount receives attention because it is the original obligatory baseline.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r16.anchor: قيل وللإعتناء بشأن الأقل لأنه الأصل الواجب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r1.claim: A further proposal repeats the conjunction as in either Zayd or Amr, but the author calls it strained: the exception normally precedes a substitute, and the pronoun should refer to the nearest half after the exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r1.anchor: كرر على نحو أكرم أما زيدا أو عمرا وتعقب بأن فيه تكلفا لأن تقديم الإستثناء على البدل ظاهر في أن البدل من الحاصل بعد الإستثناء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r2.claim: This parsing also makes decrease a concession and increase a transfer from the original measure, so the obligatory baseline should receive priority.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r2.anchor: ولأن الظاهر على هذا رجوع الضميرين إلى النصف بعد الإستثناء لأنه السابق لا النصف المطلق وأيضا الظاهر أن النقصان رخصة لأن الزيادة نقل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r4.claim: The objection that decrease is a concession is disputed: the choice may not be genuine, as in the example of completing ten with an added amount from another source.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r4.anchor: واعترض قوله الظاهر أن النقصان رخصة بأنه محل نظر إذ الظاهر أنه من قبيل أتممت عشرا فمن عندك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r5.claim: Another proposal makes the second little a quarter and its increase an eighth, yielding choices of one-half, one-quarter, or three-eighths; a 16-hour night would mean eight, four, or six hours.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r5.anchor: ومآله قم نصف الليل أو نصف نصفه أو زد على نصف النصف نصف نصف النصف فيكون التخيير فيما إذا كان ست عشرة ساعة مثلا بين قيام ثماني ساعات وأربع وست

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r6.claim: The unrestricted wording of increase suggests that it is not limited to another little; if it were, the earlier decrease could also have been stated without repeating little.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الإطلاق في أو زد عليه ظاهر الإشعار بأنه غير مقيد بقليلا إذ لو كان للإستغناء لاكتفى في أو انقص الخ بالأول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r13.speaker: التبريزي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r13.claim: On al-Tabrizi's account the exception is from the commanded two-thirds, half substitutes for little, and decrease or increase is measured against that command; the author dismisses it as implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r13.anchor: فصار القليل مفسرا بالنصف من الثلثين وهو قليل على ما تقدم أو أنقص منه أي من المأمور به

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.claim: After reviewing the many strained constructions, the author prefers his first interpretation as clearest, least contrived, and most fitting to the Qur'an's eloquence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.anchor: وأظهر الوجوه عندي وأبعدها عن التكلف وأليقها بجزالة التنزيل هو ما ذكرناه أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r16.claim: During the night prayer, recite the Qur'an deliberately and patiently, articulating letters so distinctly a listener can count them; tartīl is likened to well-spaced teeth.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r16.anchor: أي في أثناء ما ذكر من القيام أي أقرأه على تؤدة وتمهل وتبيين حروف ترتيلا بليغا بحيث يتمكن السامع من عدها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r17.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r17.claim: A report in al-ʿAskari's admonitions says the Prophet explained tartīl as clear articulation, not scattering it like dates or rushing it like poetry; dwell on its marvels, stir hearts, and do not focus only on the final sūra.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r17.anchor: وأخرج العسكري في المواعظ عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم سئل عن هذه الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says tartīl means making recitation clear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r2.anchor: ابن عباس: بينه بيانا. وقال الحسن:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to read distinctly and clearly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: اقرأه قراءة بينة. وقال مجاهد: ترسل فيه ترسلا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ترسل فيه ترسلا. وقال قتادة: تثبت فيه تثبتا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r5.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r5.claim: Qatādah says to recite deliberately and steadily.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: تثبت فيه تثبتا. وعن ابن عباس أيضا:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to read at ease in groups of three, four, or five verses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: اقرأه على هينتك ثلاث آيات أو أربعا أو خمسا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r7.speaker: أنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r7.claim: Anas says the Prophet lengthened each word in the basmalah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قال: سئل أنس كيف كانت قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: كانت مدا مدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r8.claim: Abū Wāʾil reports Ibn Masʿūd rebuked a man for reciting Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿah; the Prophet paired similar sūrahs two by two.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r8.anchor: سمعت أبا وائل قال: جاء رجل إلى ابن مسعود، قال: قرأت المفصل الليلة في ركعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says not to scatter the Qurʾān like bad dates or hurry through like poetry; pause at its wonders, move hearts, and do not focus only on the end.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله -يعني ابن مسعود -قال: لا تنثروه نثر الدقل ولا تهذوه هذ الشعر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r10.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r10.claim: Sahl reports the Prophet urged reading before people merely perfect letters like an arrow without letting Qurʾān pass their throats, and hasten its end.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r10.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي قال: بينا نحن نقرأ إذ خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:3-4/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:3-4/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:3-4/r5.claim: Recite slowly and distinctly, articulating letters so the listener can count them; the wording is likened to well spaced teeth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:3-4/r5.anchor: اقرأه على تؤدة وتبيين حروف بحيث يتمكن السامع من عدها من قوله ثغر رتل ورتل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r1.claim: Tartīl means reciting calmly and articulating letters so the listener can count them; like well-spaced teeth, the measured recitation prompts reflection and discloses difficult meanings and hidden secrets.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r1.anchor: أي اقرأه على تؤدة وبين حروفه بحيث يتمكن السامع من عدها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd warns against scattering the Qurʾān like dates or rushing it like poetry; pause at its marvels, move hearts with it, and do not focus on reaching the sūra's end.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r2.anchor: ولا تنثروه نثر الدقل ولا تهذوه هذ الشهر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r3.claim: Repeating tartīl as a verbal noun emphasizes the honor and importance of measured Qurʾān recitation.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r4.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from ʿĀʾisha that the Prophet prayed through the night repeating one verse, which asks God to punish or forgive His servants and names Him Mighty and Wise.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r4.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قام حتى أصبح بآية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r5.claim: The command sets a general manner of recitation beyond night prayer and shows that prayer's animating core is Qurʾān recitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r5.anchor: أمر بالقيام وقدر وقته وعينه , أمر بهيئة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r6.claim: The Prophet and his community need steadfastness in prophethood's work and in following its commands and prohibitions; people cannot sustain this without divine aid and diligent service that purifies the soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p205/r6.anchor: ولما كان المراد منه صلى الله عليه وسلم الثبات للنبوة ومن أمته الثبات في الاقتداء به

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r1.claim: Qatada glosses tartil as making the recitation clear.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} قال: بينه تبيينا

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says to recite the Qur'an clearly.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} قال: اقرأه قراءة بينة

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r3.claim: Mujahid explains tartil as reciting one portion after another.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} قال: بعضه على أثر بعض

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses tartil as explaining it clearly.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} قال: فسره تفسيرا

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r5.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r5.claim: Ali reports the Prophet's instruction to articulate the Qur'an, avoid scattering or rushing it like verse, pause at its wonders, move hearts, and not focus only on finishing a sura.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r5.anchor: عن علي: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن قول الله: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} قال: بينه تبيينا ولا تنثره نثر الدقل

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r6.speaker: بعض أزواج النبي
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r6.claim: A wife of the Prophet said listeners could not reproduce his recitation, then demonstrated his measured pace.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r6.anchor: عن أبي مليكة عن بعض أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنها سئلت عن قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r7.speaker: طاووس
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r7.claim: The Prophet says the best reciter is one whose recitation lets a listener see that he fears God.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r7.anchor: عن طاوس قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الناس أحسن قراءة قال: الذي إذا سمعته يقرأ رأيت أنه يخشى الله

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r8.claim: A Companion saw a man weeping and repeating a verse and identified this as the tartil commanded by the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r8.anchor: عن الحسن قال: مر رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على رجل يقرأ آية ويبكي ويرددها

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة أو أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r9.claim: The Qur'an's companion will be told on Judgment Day to recite and ascend to the station of his last recited verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أو أبي سعيد قال: يقال لصاحب القرآن يوم القيامة اقرأ وأرق فإن منزلتك عند آخر آية

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r10.claim: Mujahid says the Qur'an intercedes for its companion, who stayed awake and restrained desires for it; the person receives God's pleasure, then rises a degree and gains a reward for each verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: القرآن يشفع لصاحبه يوم القيامة يقول: يا رب جعلتني في جوفه فأسهرت ليله

DURR-FULL:v8p314/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r11.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak urges teaching Qur'an to children and families and says angels help a deceased Muslim ascend through Paradise as far as his Qur'anic knowledge reaches.
DURR-FULL:v8p314/r11.anchor: عن الضحاك بن قيس قال: يا أيها الناس علموا أولادكم وأهاليكم القرآن

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains tartil as making the recitation clear.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : ورتل القران ترتيلا قال : بينه تبيينا .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r12.claim: The pronouns in minhu and ʿalayhi refer back to al-niṣf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r12.anchor: والضمير في منه وعليه عائدان على النصف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r13.claim: In Arabic, tartīl means taking one's time and distinguishing the letters clearly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r13.anchor: ورتل القرآن معناه في اللغة تمهل وفرق بين الحروف لتبين.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r14.claim: Measured recitation gives the mind room to consider and understand meanings, softening the heart and bringing light and mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r14.anchor: والمقصد أن يجد الفكر فسحة للنظر وفهم المعاني، وبذلك يرق القلب ويفيض عليه النور والرحمة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r15.speaker: ابن كيسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r15.claim: Ibn Kaysān says the command means to understand the Qur'an while reciting; he compares the root to teeth with spaces between them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r15.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: المراد تفهمه تاليا له ومنه الثغر الرتل الذي بينه فسخ وفتوح.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r16.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r16.claim: The Prophet's recitation was clear and measured enough that a listener could count the letters if he wished.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r16.anchor: وروي أن قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت بينة مترسلة لو شاء أحد أن يعد الحروف لعدها.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r1.claim: Or increase means add time beyond half the night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r1.anchor: أو زد عليه أي على النصف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r2.claim: The commentators say the amount could range from one-third to two-thirds, leaving flexibility because the Prophet and his companions struggled and feared miscounting the required portion, sometimes standing all night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون انقص من النصف إلى الثلث أو زد عليه إلى الثلثين فجعل له سعة في مدة قيامه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r9.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers to his earlier explanation of tartil at al-Furqan 25:32.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى ورتل القرآن قد ذكرنا الترتيل في الفرقان 32

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r3.claim: Recite the Quran slowly and distinctly, which helps understanding and reflection; this was the Prophet's practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r3.anchor: أي: اقرأه على تمهل، فإنه يكون عونا على فهم القرآن وتدبره.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r4.claim: Aisha says the Prophet recited a sura with measured pacing until it lasted longer than another sura that was longer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r4.anchor: قالت عائشة: كان يقرأ السورة فيرتلها، حتى تكون أطول من أطول منها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r5.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r5.claim: Anas describes the Prophet's reading as prolonged; he demonstrated by lengthening each syllable of the basmala.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r5.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري، عن أنس: أنه سئل عن قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: كانت مدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r6.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r6.claim: Umm Salama says the Prophet paused at each verse while reciting, and she gives the opening verses as an example; Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r6.anchor: عن أم سلمة: أنها سئلت عن قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالت: كان يقطع قراءته آية آية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r7.claim: The Prophet tells the Quran's companion to recite and ascend, measuredly as in worldly life; one's station is at the last verse recited. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يقال لصاحب (3) القرآن: اقرأ وارق، ورتل كما كنت ترتل في الدنيا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls reports recommending beautiful Quran recitation and melodic voice, including the Prophet's praise of Abu Musa's Davidic-sounding voice and Abu Musa's wish to embellish his reading for him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r8.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث: "زينوا القرآن بأصواتكم"، و "ليس منا من لم يتغن بالقرآن"، و "لقد أوتي هذا مزمار من مزامير آل داود" يعني: أبا موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r9.claim: Ibn Masud says not to scatter the Quran like sand or rush it like poetry; pause at its wonders, stir hearts with it, and do not make finishing the sura one's only aim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r9.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أنه قال: لا تنثروه نثر الرمل (6) ولا تهذوه هذ الشعر، قفوا عند عجائبه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r10.speaker: أبو وائل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r10.claim: A man told Ibn Masud he had recited al-Mufassal in one rakah; Ibn Masud called that hasty as poetry and recalled that the Prophet paired twenty short suras, two in each rakah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p250/r10.anchor: سمعت أبا وائل قال: جاء رجل إلى ابن مسعود فقال: قرأت المفصل (8) الليلة في ركعة. فقال: هذا كهذ الشعر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.claim: In another report Aisha says the Prophet came out displeased when people gathered to follow his night prayer, compassionately fearing that the vigil would become obligatory; he urged them to do only what they could sustain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كنت أجعل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصيرا يصلي عليه من الليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r3.claim: Aisha’s report says the people maintained the vigil intensely for eight months, after which God showed mercy, restored the obligatory prayers, and left night prayer voluntary; it also says the best deeds are those done consistently.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r1.claim: The earlier night-vigil obligation was abrogated by the later instruction to recite what is easy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r1.anchor: ثم نسخ ذلك بقوله تعالى : ( علم أن لن تحصوه فتاب عليكم فاقرؤوا ما تيسر من القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Aslam gloss tartīl as making the Qur'an clear in recitation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r2.anchor: بين القرآن تبيانا , قاله ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr glosses the command as interpreting or explaining the Qur'an.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r4.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r4.claim: Ibn Baḥr says to read in sequence without altering wording or advancing what comes later, deriving the image from evenly arranged teeth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r4.anchor: لا تغير لفظا ولا تقدم مؤخرا مأخوذ من ترتيل الأسنان إذا استوى نبتها وحسن انتظامها , قاله ابن بحر

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r10.claim: The Prophet may pray half the night, somewhat less down toward a third, or more up toward two-thirds.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r10.anchor: فالمعنى تخييره عليه السلام بين أن يقوم نصفه أو أقل منه أو أكثر أي قم إلى الصلاة في الزمان المحدود

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r11.claim: Some relate the options to seasonal night length: half when night and day are equal, less when nights shorten, and more when they lengthen.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r11.anchor: قيل هذا التخيير على حسب طول الليالي وقصرها فالنصف إذا استوى ليل والنهار والنقص منه إذا أقصر الليل

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r12.claim: Recite during the night vigil slowly and distinctly, articulating the letters so that they do not run into one another.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r12.anchor: أي أقرأه على تؤدة وتبيين حروف وبالفارسية وقر آرا كشده

MUQATIL:73:1-6/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r5.anchor: ترسل به ترسلا على هينتك رويدا يعني عز وجل بينه تبينا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r1.claim: Increasing the half means raising it to two thirds.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r2.claim: If “half” is appositive to “a little,” the options are three: a full half, less than half, or more than half; otherwise the choice is a fixed amount below half or a choice to decrease or increase it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r2.anchor: والمراد التخيير بين أمرين بين أين يقوم أقل من نصف الليل على البت وبين ان يختار أحد الأمرين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r3.claim: Half is called little relative to the whole; in ordinary usage “a little” means less than half, as when all but a little of a thousand is owed, more than half remains due.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r3.anchor: وإنا وصف النصف بالقلة بالنسبة إلى الكل وإلا فاطلاق لفظ القليل ينطلق على ما دون النصف

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r4.claim: Rattala means to articulate and distinguish; the word evokes evenly spaced teeth and well-proportioned speech.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r4.anchor: بين وفصل من الثغر المرتل أي المفلج الأسنان وكلام رتل بالتحريك أي مرتل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r5.claim: Recite deliberately, articulating letters, observing pauses, and fully pronouncing the vowels.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r5.anchor: أو اقرأ على تؤدة بتبيين الحروف وحفظ الوقوف واشباع الحركات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r6.claim: The verbal noun intensifies the command and indicates that measured recitation is necessary for the reader.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#3/r6.anchor: هو تأكيد في إيجاب الامر به وانه لا بد منه للقارئ

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r1.speaker: أبو داود
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r1.claim: A report collected by Abū Dāwūd says the Qurʾān reciter will be told in Paradise to read, ascend, and recite as in worldly life; the reciter’s rank is at the last verse read.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r1.anchor: خرجه أبو داود وقد تقدم في أول الكتاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r2.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r2.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet used to lengthen his voice while reciting.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4#2/r2.anchor: وروى أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يمد صوته بالقراءة مدا.

QASHANI:73:1-4/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:73:1-4/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:73:1-4/r5.claim: For the weak, increase it to two thirds, leaving one third each for rest, necessities, and devotion to God and the spiritual path.
QASHANI:73:1-4/r5.anchor: إن كنت من الضعفاء حتى يصير إلى الثلثين

QASHANI:73:1-4/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:73:1-4/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:73:1-4/r6.claim: Reciting the Quran distinctly means bringing forth, through purification, the meanings and realities gathered in primordial nature and hidden in one’s potential.
QASHANI:73:1-4/r6.anchor: فصل ما في فطرتك من المعاني والحقائق مجموعة

RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains tartil as clear articulation: it cannot be achieved by rushing, but requires distinguishing every letter and giving it its due length.
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r1.anchor: والتبيين لا يتم بأن يعجل في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r2.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad relates tartil to teeth spaced apart without much gap.
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r2.anchor: إذا كان بين الثنايا افتراق ليس بالكثير

RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r3.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r3.claim: Al-Layth says tartil is arranging something; well-set teeth are ratl, and rattalt al-kalam means reciting slowly and composing speech well.
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r3.anchor: قال الليث : الترتيل تنسيق الشيء ، وثغر رتل

RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r4.claim: The verbal noun tartīlan reinforces that the command is binding and indispensable for the reciter.
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r4.anchor: وأنه مما لا بد منه للقارىء

RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r5.claim: After ordering night prayer, God commands measured recitation so the mind can contemplate each verse's truths and subtleties, feel divine majesty, and respond to promise and threat with hope and fear.
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r5.anchor: حتى يتمكن الخاطر من التأمل في حقائق تلك الآيات ودقائقها

RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r6.claim: Such reflection illuminates the heart with knowledge of God; haste signals failure to attend to meanings, since one who loves a thing does not rush its mention, so tartil aims at presence of heart and perfected knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v30p153/r6.anchor: فظهر أن المقصود من الترتيل إنما هو حضور القلب وكما المعرفة

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r1.claim: These are the earliest-revealed verses explicitly to enjoin Quran recitation as worship, a command repeated in other passages.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r1.anchor: These are the first verses in the chronological order of revelation to explicitly enjoin reciting the Quran as a form of worship

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r2.claim: The measured-recitation command may apply to all Muslims or specifically to the Prophet as he delivers revelation to others.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r2.anchor: The command to recite the Quran in a measured pace can be seen as an injunction for all Muslims or as one that applies specifically to the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r3.claim: The Prophet’s measured recitation reflects God’s own description of how He recited revelation to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r3.anchor: In this way the Prophet’s manner of recitation reflects the manner that God ascribes to Himself in 25:32

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r4.speaker: Umm Salamah
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r4.claim: Umm Salamah reports that the Prophet recited verse by verse, pausing at each verse’s end.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r4.anchor: his wife Umm Salamah is reported to have said, “He used to divide his recitation verse by verse”

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r5.claim: The Prophet urged his followers to adorn the Quran with their voices.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r5.anchor: The Prophet enjoined his followers to recite the Quran, saying, “Adorn the Quran with your voices”

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r6.claim: The Prophet says that one who does not chant the Quran is not one of his followers.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r6.anchor: The Prophet enjoined his followers to recite the Quran

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r7.speaker: aḥādīth
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r7.claim: A report promises that fluent Quran reciters accompany the honorable, obedient angelic scribes, while those who recite with difficulty receive double reward.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r7.anchor: Whosoever recites the Quran fluently is with the honorable and obedient scribes [i.e., the angels], and whosoever recites it with difficulty shall receive a double reward

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r8.speaker: aḥādīth
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r8.claim: A report promises peace, mercy, angelic attendance, and God’s remembrance for a group gathered in a house of God to recite and contemplate scripture.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r8.anchor: Never does a group gather in one of the houses of God, reciting the Book of God and contemplating it, but that peace descends upon them

STUDYQURAN:73:3/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r9.speaker: a famous ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r9.claim: A famous report likens the believer who recites Quran to a sweet citrus fruit and the nonreciting believer to a sweet dried date; the reciting hypocrite is fragrant but bitter, while the nonreciting hypocrite is bitter apple.
STUDYQURAN:73:3/r9.anchor: Regarding the different levels of recitation, a famousḥadīth states

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.claim: Night vigil was initially obligatory, with the Prophet allowed to pray approximately one-third to one-half of the night or somewhat more; after the five prayers became obligatory it was abrogated for the community but remained obligatory for him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.anchor: قم نصف الليل ، وأنقص من النصف

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r10.claim: Tartīl means letting the inner self dwell on the Qur'an's meaning and reciting slowly with the tongue.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r10.anchor: ارتع بسرك في فهمه ، وتأن بلسانك في قراءته

TAB-FULL:v23p362/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r2.claim: The alternatives are to stand half the night, shorten it slightly, or lengthen it; God gave this choice when prescribing night prayer.
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، قال لما نزلت {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] الآية، قام المسلمون حولا، فمنهم من أطاقه

TAB-FULL:v23p364/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r1.claim: Recite the Qur'an clearly and distinctly, at a measured pace.
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 4] قال: اقرأه قراءة بينة

TAB-FULL:v23p364/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses tartil as reciting clearly.
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 4] قال: اقرأه قراءة بينة

TAB-FULL:v23p364/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r3.claim: Mujahid describes tartil as reading portions successively, with deliberation and without haste.
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r3.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 4] فقال: بعضه على أثر بعض، على تؤدة

TAB-FULL:v23p364/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r4.claim: Mujahid also glosses the command as proceeding slowly through the recitation.
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قول الله {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 4] قال: ترسل فيه ترسلا

TAB-FULL:v23p364/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits from Ata that tartil means al-nabdh, casting or placing something down.
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r5.anchor: قال ابن جريج، عن عطاء، {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 4] قال: الترتيل النبذ: الطرح

TAB-FULL:v23p364/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r6.claim: Qatada says tartil means making the Qur'an clear.
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 4] قال بينه بيانا

TAB-FULL:v23p364/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise glosses tartil as making the recitation clear.
TAB-FULL:v23p364/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 4] قال: بينه بيانا

SULAMI:v2p355#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p355#2/r1.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says to contemplate the subtleties of the Qur'an's address, make the self observe its rulings, the heart understand its meanings, and the innermost self turn toward it.
SULAMI:v2p355#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : تدبر لطائف خطابه وطالب نفسك بالقيام بأحكامه وقلبك بفهم معانيه وسرك

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.claim: The sura commands the Prophet to pray at night to prepare for the weighty revelation, endure opponents' abuse, and leave them graciously; it warns unbelievers, extends the ruling to believers, then eases it.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.anchor: تأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بقيام الليل والصلاة فيه ليستعد بذلك لتلقي ثقل ما سيلقى عليه من القول الثقيل

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.claim: The sura is Meccan and among the earliest revelations; it is said to be the second or third sura revealed.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.anchor: والسورة مكية من عتائق السور النازلة في أول البعثة

TABATABAI:73:4-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r3.claim: Tartil is reciting the Quran while distinctly articulating its letters in sequence.
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r3.anchor: ترتيل القرآن تلاوته بتبيين حروفه على تواليها

TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.claim: The tartil clause coordinates with the command to stand: stand at night and recite the Quran distinctly.
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.anchor: أي قم الليل واقرأ القرآن بترتيل

TABATABAI:73:4-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r5.claim: Apparently tartil means reciting in the night prayer, or refers to the prayer itself.
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بترتيل القرآن ترتيله في الصلاة أو المراد به الصلاة نفسها

TABATABAI:73:4-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r6.claim: The Quran calls prayer by a similar expression in 17:78, including the witnessed dawn recitation.
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r6.anchor: عبر سبحانه عن الصلاة بنظير هذا التعبير في قوله أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس

TABATABAI:73:4-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r7.claim: Another view reads the command as requiring Quran recitation without prayer.
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد إيجاب قراءة القرآن دون الصلاة

AKHFASH:v2p552/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p552/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p552/r2.claim: The sense inserts an omitted أو before نصفه: or half the night, or a little less, or more; Arabic can omit أو in such a sequence, as in giving one, two, or three dirhams.
AKHFASH:v2p552/r2.anchor: إنما المعنى "أو نصفه أو زد عليه" لأن ما يكون في معنى تكلم به العرب بغير: "أو"

TABRISI:73:1-10/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10/r4.claim: Tartīl carefully articulates each letter as it deserves; rapid ḥadr is also good, but tartīl is encouraged here.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r4.anchor: والترتيل ترتيب الحروف على حقها في تلاوتها بتثبت فيها والحدر هو الإسراع فيها

TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r3.claim: The command gives a range around half the night: reduce the half a little or increase it a little.
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r3.anchor: فالمعنى قم نصف الليل أو انقص من نصف الليل أو زد على نصف الليل

TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r10.speaker: المفسرون
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r10.claim: Exegetes explain reducing as going down to one third and increasing as going up to two thirds.
TABRISI:73:1-10#2/r10.anchor: وقال المفسرون أو انقص من النصف قليلا إلى الثلث أو زد على النصف إلى الثلثين

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to articulate the Qurʾan clearly and read unhurriedly in sets of three, four, or five verses.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r10.anchor: ثلاث آيات وأربعا وخمسا عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r11.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj says clarity requires not rushing: every letter must be fully articulated and given its due.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r11.anchor: والبيان لا يتم بأن تعجل في القرآن إنما يتم بأن تبين جميع الحروف

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās told Abū Ḥamza he preferred a measured reading of al-Baqara to reciting the whole Qurʾan.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r12.anchor: لأن أقرأ البقرة أرتلها أحب إلي من أن أقرأ القرآن كله

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r13.claim: Mujāhid explains tartīl as reading slowly and deliberately.

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r14.claim: Qatāda explains tartīl as reading with steadiness and deliberation.

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r15.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r15.claim: ʿAlī says not to rush like poetry or scatter like sand, but to strike hard hearts and not merely aim to finish a surah.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r15.anchor: بينه بيانا ولا تهذه هذ الشعر ولا تنثره نثر الرمل

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r16.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r16.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh says to ask God for Paradise at verses mentioning it and seek refuge from Hell at verses mentioning it.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r16.anchor: إذا مررت بآية فيها ذكر الجنة فاسأل الله الجنة

TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r1.claim: Another view says tartīl means reading in sequence without changing wording or moving later material ahead.
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r1.anchor: الترتيل هو أن تقرأ على نظمه وتواليه ولا تغير لفظا ولا تقدم مؤخرا

TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r2.claim: This explanation derives tartīl from evenly arranged teeth and a gap-free, well-ordered set of teeth.
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r2.anchor: مأخوذ من ترتل الأسنان إذا استوت وحسن انتظامها

TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r3.speaker: قطرب
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r3.claim: Quṭrub says ratl means softness, so tartīl here calls for a sorrowful tone.
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r3.anchor: رتل معناه ضعف والرتل اللين عن قطرب

TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r4.speaker: أبو بصير
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r4.claim: Abū Baṣīr reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that tartīl means lingering over verses and beautifying the voice.
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r4.anchor: ما رواه أبو بصير عن أبي عبد الله ع في هذا

TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r5.speaker: أم سلمة
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r5.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet paused his recitation verse by verse.
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r5.anchor: وروي عن أم سلمة أنها قالت: كان رسول الله

TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r6.speaker: أنس
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r6.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet prolonged his voice in recitation.
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r6.anchor: وعن أنس قال كان يمد صوته مدا

TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet's promise that the Qurʾan's companion will be told to recite and rise, with rank at the last verse read.
TABRISI:73:1-10#4/r7.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

FARRA:v3p196#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p196#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p196#2/r3.claim: The allowance is to reduce the half toward a third or increase it toward two-thirds.
FARRA:v3p196#2/r3.anchor: «أو انقص منه قليلا» (3) من النصف إلى الثلث أو زد على النصف إلى الثلثين

FARRA:v3p196#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p196#2/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p196#2/r5.claim: Recite the Qur’an calmly and unhurriedly.
FARRA:v3p196#2/r5.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: ورتل القرآن ترتيلا (4) . يقول: اقرأه على هينتك ترسلا.

THALABI:v10p59/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p59/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan calls the additional night prayer a voluntary act after an obligation.
THALABI:v10p59/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: في هذه الآية الحمد لله تطوع بعد فريضة

THALABI:v10p59/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p59/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to recite distinctly and make the meaning clear.
THALABI:v10p59/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: اقرأه قراءة، بينه تبيانا

THALABI:v10p59/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r6.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p59/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan also recommends reading at an unhurried pace of three, four, or five verses.
THALABI:v10p59/r6.anchor: وعنه أيضا: اقرأه على هينتك ثلاث آيات وأربعا وخمسا

THALABI:v10p59/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r7.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p59/r7.claim: Qatāda says to read it steadily and deliberately.
THALABI:v10p59/r7.anchor: قتادة: تثبت فيه تثبيتا. ابن كيسان: تفهمه تاليا له

THALABI:v10p59/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r8.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p59/r8.claim: Ibn Kaysān says to understand the Qurʾān while reciting it.

THALABI:v10p59/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p59/r9.claim: Another view takes tartīl as separating the verses clearly and not rushing; the source links the word to spaced teeth described as ratl.
THALABI:v10p59/r9.anchor: وقيل: فصله تفصيلا ولا تعجل في قراءته، وهو من قول العرب

THALABI:v10p59/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r10.speaker: أبو بكر ابن طاهر
THALABI:v10p59/r10.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir urges reflection on the address’s subtleties, observance of its rulings, understanding by the heart, and inward attention.
THALABI:v10p59/r10.anchor: أبو بكر ابن طاهر: دبر في لطائف خطابه، وطالب نفسك بالقيام

THALABI:v10p59/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p59/r11.claim: The Prophet says the Qurʾān’s companion will be told to recite and ascend; his station is at the last verse recited.
THALABI:v10p59/r11.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «يقال لصاحب القرآن: اقرأ وارق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains tartīl as clear explanation and articulation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r3.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: بينة بيانا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that recitation should proceed at an unhurried, comfortable pace.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r4.anchor: وروى الكلبي عنه: على هينتك (¬2) ترتيلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r5.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says to deliver the Qurʾān one letter at a time.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r6.claim: Mujāhid interprets tartīl as reciting some of it after another portion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r6.anchor: وعن مجاهد قال: بعضه في أثر بعض (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r7.claim: Qatāda says it had reached them that most of the Prophet’s recitation used lengthening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية: بلغنا أن عامة قراءة النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- (¬8) كانت بالمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r8.claim: Abū Isḥāq says clear recitation cannot be achieved by haste: all letters must be articulated and their due lengthening fulfilled.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} بينه تبيينا، والتبيين لا يتم (¬1) بأن يعجل في القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r9.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines tartīl as pausing, deliberating, and making speech intelligible, deriving it from teeth with a slight gap between them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r9.anchor: وقال المبرد: معنى الترتيل: التوقف، والتمهل، والإفهام، وأصله من قولهم: ثغر رتل (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r10.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r10.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says tartīl means precise, clear articulation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r10.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: ما أعلم الترتيل إلا التحقيق والتبيين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r11.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r11.claim: Al-Layth describes orderly arrangement and well-aligned teeth; to recite with tartīl is to speak slowly and compose speech well.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r11.anchor: (وقال) (¬7) الليث: (الرتل: تنسيق الشيء، وثغر (¬8) رتل (¬9) حسن التنضيد، ورتلت الكلام (¬10) ترتيلا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p493#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p493#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p493#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says he has already discussed reciting the Quran with measured clarity in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p493#3/r2.anchor: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} قد ذكرناه في سورة بني إسرائيل (4) .

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:1-4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:1-4/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:1-4/r4.claim: Increasing beyond half means reaching two thirds, so the options are two thirds, one half, or one third of the night.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:1-4/r4.anchor: أو زد عليه } على النصف إلى الثلثين، جعل له سعة في مدة قيامه في الليل، فكأنه قال: قم ثلثي الليل أو نصفه أو ثلثه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r1.claim: Recite distinctly and clearly, one part following another, with deliberation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r1.anchor: رتل القرآن ترتيلا } أي: بينه تبيينا بعضه على إثر بعض في تؤدة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r5.claim: The Prophet is ordered to spend much of the night in worship; verses 3–4 allow the period to be half the night, somewhat less, or somewhat more.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r5.anchor: 2. âyette Hz. Peygamber’e gecenin büyük bir kısmını ibadetle geçirmesi emredilmiş; 3 ve 4. âyetlerde ibadet süresinin, gecenin yarısı kadar, daha azı yahut biraz fazlası olabileceği belirtilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r7.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r7.claim: Most commentaries say night prayer was obligatory for the Prophet and remained so after the five daily prayers became obligatory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r7.anchor: Çoğunlukla tefsirlerde gece kalkıp namaz kılmanın Hz. Peygamber’e farz olduğu, beş vakit namaz farz kılındıktan sonra da bu ödevin aynen devam ettiği bildirilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r8.claim: The tahajjud obligation applied only to the Prophet; for his community, getting up at night for this prayer is sunnah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r8.anchor: Teheccüd adı verilen bu gece namazı yükümlülüğü Hz. Peygamber’e mahsus olup ümmetinin de geceleyin kalkıp bu namazı kılmaları sünnet kabul edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r9.claim: Tartīl lexically means arranging, ordering, bringing out, and explaining something well.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r9.anchor: tertîl, sözlükte “bir şeyi güzel bir şekilde sıralamak, dizmek, açığa çıkarmak ve açıklamak” anlamlarına gelmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r10.claim: Here tartīl means reciting the Qur'an clearly, correctly, distinctly, and slowly while reflecting on its meaning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r10.anchor: Burada Kur’an’ın açık ve düzgün bir şekilde, tane tane ve yavaş yavaş, mânası üzerinde düşünerek okunması kastedilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r11.claim: God commands measured recitation because it better supports understanding the Qur'an and reflecting on its meanings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r11.anchor: Bu şekilde okumak Kur’an’ı anlamaya ve mânalarını düşünmeye daha elverişli olduğu için yüce Allah böyle okunmasını emretmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r12.speaker: İbn Kesîr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r12.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the Qur'an slowly, giving each letter its due.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r12.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in Kur’an’ı, harflerinin hakkını vererek ağır ağır okuduğu rivayet edilir (İbn Kesîr, VIII, 276).

BURHAN:v3p35/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p35/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p35/r4.claim: ترتيلا conveys abundant reading in a measured, reflective manner, whereas وما علمناه الشعر denies the basic act of teaching poetry rather than intensifying its negation.
BURHAN:v3p35/r4.anchor: يدل على كثرة القراءة على هيئة التأني والتدبر

ITQAN:v1p221/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p221/r1.claim: The science of stopping and beginning in recitation was treated in dedicated works and teaches proper performance of reading.
ITQAN:v1p221/r1.anchor: وهو فن جليل به يعرف كيف أداء القراءة

ITQAN:v1p221/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p221/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
ITQAN:v1p221/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the Companions learned each surah's lawful and forbidden matters and where to stop, unlike readers who recite without grasping commands or pauses; al-Naḥḥās takes this as evidence that they learned pauses with the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v1p221/r2.anchor: لقد عشنا برهة من دهرنا وإن أحدنا ليؤتى الإيمان قبل القرآن

ITQAN:v1p221/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p221/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p221/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar's wording that they lived through an earlier period indicates consensus among the Companions on learning stopping points; al-Bayhaqī transmits the report.
ITQAN:v1p221/r3.anchor: وقول ابن عمر لقد عشنا برهة من دهرنا يدل على أن ذلك إجماع من الصحابة ثابت

ITQAN:v1p221/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p221/r4.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v1p221/r4.claim: ʿAlī defines tartīl as articulating the letters well and knowing where to pause.
ITQAN:v1p221/r4.anchor: وعن علي في قوله تعالى ﴿ ورتل القرآن ترتيلا ﴾ قال الترتيل تجويد الحروف ومعرفة الوقوف

ITQAN:v1p221/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p221/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ITQAN:v1p221/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says knowledge of stopping and beginning is part of complete knowledge of the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v1p221/r5.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري من تمام معرفة القرآن معرفة الوقف والابتداء فيه

ITQAN:v1p221/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p221/r6.speaker: النكزاوي
ITQAN:v1p221/r6.claim: Al-Nakzāwī says meanings and legal deductions cannot be properly known without understanding verse boundaries, making the science of stopping important.
ITQAN:v1p221/r6.anchor: وقال النكزاوي باب الوقف عظيم القدر جليل الخطر

ITQAN:v1p221/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p221/r7.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p221/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī argues that breath requires chosen pauses and suitable restarting; pauses must preserve meaning, reveal inimitability, and fulfill intent. The imams urged mastery, and many later authorities required it for certification.
ITQAN:v1p221/r7.anchor: إذ بذلك يظهر الإعجاز ويحصل القصد ولذلك حض الأئمة على تعلمه ومعرفته

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r1.claim: Tartīl is recommended in Qur'an recitation.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r1.anchor: يسن الترتيل في قراءة القرآن قال تعالى ﴿ ورتل القرآن ترتيلا ﴾

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r2.claim: Umm Salama describes the Prophet's recitation as clear and articulated, letter by letter.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r2.anchor: عن أم سلمة أنها نعتت قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قراءة مفسرة حرفا حرفا

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r3.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r3.claim: Anas says the Prophet's recitation was measured, illustrating his elongation of the words Allah, al-Raḥmān, and al-Raḥīm in the basmala.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r3.anchor: عن أنس أنه سئل عن قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال كانت مدا

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r4.claim: In the Ṣaḥīḥayn, Ibn Masʿūd rebukes reciting the entire Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿa as hasty like poetry; recitation that reaches and settles in the heart benefits.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أن رجلا قال له إني أقرأ المفصل في ركعة واحدة فقال هذا كهذ الشعر

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says not to scatter or rush the Qur'an like poetry, but to pause at its wonders, move hearts with it, and not make finishing the surah one's sole aim.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال لا تنثروه نثر الدقل ولا تهذوه هذا الشعر

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic report promises the Qur'an's companion rising through ranks while reciting with tartīl; the final rank corresponds to the last verse recited.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r6.anchor: من حديث ابن عمر مرفوعا يقال لصاحب القرآن اقرأ وارق في الدرجات ورتل كما كنت ترتل في الدنيا

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r7.speaker: أصحاب شرح المهذب
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r7.claim: The jurists cited in Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab agree that excessive haste in recitation is disliked.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r7.anchor: قال في شرح المهذب واتفقوا على كراهة الإفراط في الإسراع

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r8.claim: The cited scholars judge reciting one portion with tartīl better than reading two portions in the same time without tartīl.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r8.anchor: وقراءة جزء بترتيل أفضل من قراءة جزئين في قدر ذلك الزمان بلا ترتيل

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r9.claim: Tartīl supports reflection, reverence, and a stronger effect on the heart; it is recommended even for a non-Arab who does not understand the meaning.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r9.anchor: واستحباب الترتيل للتدبر ولأنه أقرب إلى الإجلال والتوقير وأشد تأثيرا في القلب

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r10.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r10.claim: Authorities differ over slower tartīl versus faster, more numerous recitation; one reconciliation gives tartīl greater reward in quality, while quantity earns more tenfold rewards per letter.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r10.anchor: إن ثواب قراءة الترتيل أجل قدرا وثواب الكثرة أكثر عددا لأن بكل حرف عشر حسنات

ITQAN:v1p282#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r11.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r11.claim: Al-Zarkashī defines full tartīl as clear, emphatic articulation without merging letters; its fullest form matches delivery to meaning, voicing threats as threats and glorification with reverence.
ITQAN:v1p282#2/r11.anchor: كمال الترتيل تفخيم ألفاظه والإبانة عن حروفه وألا يدغم حرف في حرف

BURHAN:v1p449/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p449/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p449/r1.claim: The Quran is the lasting greatest miracle and proof in every age; its reader should treat it as a major divine gift and ensure it testifies for, not against, them.
BURHAN:v1p449/r1.anchor: بكونه أعظم المعجزات لبقائه ببقاء دعوة الاسلام

BURHAN:v1p449/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p449/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p449/r2.claim: The reader should remember the commands, prohibitions, and cautionary histories in the Quran, avoiding the disobedience that ruined those who became examples.
BURHAN:v1p449/r2.anchor: لأن القرآن مشتمل على طلب أمور والكف عن أمور

BURHAN:v1p449/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p449/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p449/r3.claim: Every Muslim reciting the Quran must use tartil; its minimum includes clear articulation, full pronunciation, measured breathing, reflection, and avoiding elision between letters.
BURHAN:v1p449/r3.anchor: فحق على كل امرىء مسلم قرأ القرآن أن يرتله

BURHAN:v1p449/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p449/r4.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v1p449/r4.claim: Another view sets minimum tartil as making the recitation clear even when hurried; its fullest form pauses without stretching or dragging the reading.
BURHAN:v1p449/r4.anchor: وقيل أقل الترتيل أن يأتي بما يبين ما يقرأ به وإن كان مستعجلا في قراءته

BURHAN:v1p449/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p449/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p449/r5.claim: The reader should match delivery to each passage, voicing threats like someone issuing a threat and words of reverence with reverence.
BURHAN:v1p449/r5.anchor: فإن كان يقرأ تهديدا لفظ به لفظ المتهدد وإن كان يقرأ لفظ تعظيم لفظ به على التعظيم

BURHAN:v1p449/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p449/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p449/r6.claim: Reflect on each verse before moving on: pause at mercy to rejoice and ask for Paradise, and at punishment to heed its warning and seek refuge from the Fire.
BURHAN:v1p449/r6.anchor: فإذا مر به آية رحمة وقف عندها وفرح بما وعده الله تعالى منها

NASHR:v1p208/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p208/r9.speaker: علي
NASHR:v1p208/r9.claim: Ali defines tartil as articulating the letters well and knowing where to pause.
NASHR:v1p208/r9.anchor: وجاء عن علي - رضي الله عنه - أنه سئل عن قوله تعالى: ورتل القرآن ترتيلا فقال: الترتيل تجويد الحروف
